problem: Flow map models remain unstable and expensive to train, sensitive to hyperparameters even when initialized from pre-trained diffusion models.
approach: Introduces mid-training, a lightweight intermediate stage between diffusion pre-training and flow map post-training that learns trajectory-consistent initialization for vision generation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art two-step FIDs (1.97 on CIFAR-10, 1.32 on ImageNet 64×64, 1.84 on ImageNet 512×512) using up to 98% less training data and GPU time than prior methods.

problem: Open-ended scientific problem solving is inherently unbounded and domain-specific, requiring exploration across vast solution spaces with limited generalization in existing approaches.
approach: Proposes HELIX, a hierarchical evolutionary reinforcement learning framework combining diverse candidate solutions through in-context learning with iterative RL policy refinement.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on circle packing (sum of radii 2.635983 using 14B model) and surpasses GPT-4o on ML benchmarks with 5.95-point F1 improvement on Adult/Bank Marketing and 40.5% RMSE reduction on Boston Housing.

problem: Federated LLM fine-tuning faces massive memory and communication challenges due to parameter scale, while non-IID data across clients further complicates convergence.
approach: Introduces Meerkat, a sparse zeroth-order optimization method using transferable static parameter subsets with high-frequency communication and virtual path mechanisms to detect extreme Non-IID clients.
contribution: Enables cost-effective federated LLM fine-tuning with superior performance compared to full-parameter zeroth-order baselines and improved handling of data heterogeneity.

problem: Contact forces in robot dynamics introduce discontinuities that severely degrade gradient-based optimization in simulators, creating a trade-off between realism and gradient accuracy.
approach: Proposes DiffMJX coupling adaptive time integration with penalty-based simulation, plus contacts from distance (CFD) using straight-through estimation to preserve pre-contact gradients.
contribution: Substantially improves gradient accuracy under hard contacts and enables informative pre-contact gradients while maintaining physical realism.

problem: PDE surrogate models like FNO and PINN fail to generalize across inputs with diverse physical units and scales, severely limiting out-of-distribution prediction.
approach: Proposes π-invariant test-time projection preserving Buckingham π-invariants via log-space least squares, with clustering to reduce computational complexity from O(MN) to O(KN).
contribution: Achieves average MAE reduction up to 91% across wide input scale ranges on 2D thermal conduction and linear elasticity with minimal overhead.

problem: Small proxy models trained with fixed hyperparameters produce unreliable dataset rankings for pretraining data selection, with conclusions not transferring to large-scale production.
approach: Proposes training proxy models with sufficiently small learning rates to produce dataset rankings that correlate with large-scale optimally-tuned models, with theoretical guarantee via random-feature analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates through 23 data recipes that small-scale ranking reliability can be recovered with proper hyperparameter tuning, preventing costly data selection errors.

problem: Dynamical Similarity Analysis (DSA) ignores how inputs drive dynamics, misclassifying similar systems driven differently—a critical issue for real-world non-autonomous systems.
approach: Introduces InputDSA extending DSA by estimating and comparing both input and intrinsic dynamic operators using Dynamic Mode Decomposition with control (DMDc) based on subspace identification.
contribution: Successfully compares partially observed input-driven systems from noisy data and identifies that high-performing RNNs are dynamically similar while low-performing ones are more diverse.

problem: Large reasoning models produce plausible-sounding but unreliable rationales that fail to reflect their true decision process, undermining trustworthiness and reliability.
approach: Introduces RFEval benchmark with 7,186 instances across seven tasks using controlled output-level counterfactual interventions to probe two testable conditions: stance consistency and causal influence.
contribution: Finds unfaithfulness in 49.7% of outputs from twelve open-source LRMs, reveals that post-training RL can reduce faithfulness despite maintaining accuracy, and proves accuracy is not a reliable proxy for faithfulness.

problem: Existing static agent benchmarks rapidly saturate as agents improve, failing to provide sustained evaluation challenges and limiting ability to assess emerging capabilities.
approach: Proposes TRACE framework where agents freely explore and evolve original benchmark tasks into higher-difficulty variants while recording traceable execution trajectories through evolutionary proposal mining and multi-level validation.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent task complexity enhancement on GAIA benchmark with improved correctness reliability through validatable reproducible trajectories, enabling self-evolving evaluation systems.

problem: Estimating Schrodinger potentials for optimal transport between distributions lacks tight sample complexity guarantees when only observing samples from initial and final densities.
approach: Uses Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference process with stochastic optimal control to estimate Schrodinger potentials, deriving tight generalization bounds under spectral assumptions via risk minimization.
contribution: Establishes tight bounds on generalization ability achieving fast convergence rates up to logarithmic factors for Schrodinger potential estimation including Gaussian mixtures.

problem: Multi-view 3D generation suffers from poor visual quality while 3D-consistent approaches sacrifice realism, with conventional multi-view paradigm unable to balance these trade-offs efficiently.
approach: Proposes FlashWorld with dual-mode pre-training from video diffusion priors followed by cross-mode post-training distillation that bridges multi-view and 3D-oriented generation while reducing denoising steps.
contribution: Generates high-quality 3D scenes from single image or text in seconds, 10-100x faster than prior works while maintaining superior rendering quality and 3D consistency.

problem: Claims of optimizer speedups are undermined by unequal hyperparameter tuning and limited evaluation, obscuring fair comparisons and hindering practical adoption of alternatives to AdamW.
approach: Conducts systematic study of ten optimizers across four model scales and data-to-model ratios with rigorous hyperparameter tuning and evaluations at training end, revealing matrix-based preconditioners as fastest methods.
contribution: Shows actual speedup of proposed optimizers over well-tuned AdamW decreases with scale to 1.1x for 1.2B models, with matrix-based optimizers (Muon/Soap) being fastest but speedup inversely proportional to scale.

problem: Vision-language models struggle with visual-spatial reasoning because visual tokens are overshadowed by language tokens, preventing consistent recognition of visual cues across frames.
approach: Proposes VideoAnchor, a plug-and-play module leveraging sparse subspace clustering's self-expressiveness property to reinforce visual cues via attention anchoring without retraining.
contribution: Achieves 3.2% and 4.6% improvements on VSI-Bench and Video-MME spatial-related tasks with InternVL2-8B and Qwen2.5VL-72B respectively, demonstrating consistent gains across models.

problem: Understanding how Transformers learn from long, distributional contexts and recall relevant information remains theoretically unclear despite empirical success in content-addressable retrieval.
approach: Recasts Transformer attention as measure-theoretic associative memory where context is a distribution and attention is an integral operator, proving softmax attention trained via empirical risk minimization learns recall-and-predict decomposition.
contribution: Establishes matching minimax lower bounds proving convergence optimality, providing theoretical grounding for Transformer generalization on long distributional contexts.

problem: Existing mechanistic interpretability and circuit discovery rely on manual inspection at toy scale and miss feature interactions through activation-only analysis.
approach: Proposes WeightLens and CircuitLens that analyze features directly from learned weights and capture circuit-level dynamics via transcoders, eliminating need for explainer models or datasets.
contribution: Increases interpretability robustness by going beyond activation analysis to reveal circuit dynamics, enhancing scalable mechanistic analysis while maintaining efficiency.

problem: Visual-prompted object detection lacks research and relies on text-prompted training, leading to suboptimal performance from missing global discriminability in visual prompts despite advantages for rare categories.
approach: Proposes DETR-ViP combining image-text contrastive learning with global prompt integration, visual-textual prompt relation distillation, and selective fusion strategy for robust detection.
contribution: Substantially outperforms state-of-the-art on COCO, LVIS, ODinW, and Roboflow100 benchmarks with enhanced discriminative visual prompt representations.

problem: Multi-agent coordination faces trade-off between capturing diverse behaviors and enabling real-time execution: diffusion methods excel at expressiveness but are computationally slow.
approach: Proposes MAC-Flow learning flow-based representation of joint behaviors then distilling into decentralized one-step policies via flow matching for fast execution.
contribution: Achieves 14.5x faster inference compared to diffusion-based MARL methods while maintaining performance across 12 environments and 34 datasets.

problem: Large-scale TSP remains NP-hard and unsolved efficiently: classical methods don't scale, heuristics need domain tuning, and learning methods generalize poorly with fixed training.
approach: Proposes ViTSP leveraging pre-trained VLMs to visually identify promising small-scale subproblems from TSP visualization, then solving with off-the-shelf optimizer for global improvement.
contribution: Achieves sub-0.2% average optimality gaps on instances up to 88k nodes, surpassing LKH-3 by 12-100% gap reduction especially on very-large-scale instances.

problem: Attribute correlations in training data prevent deep generative models from synthesizing under-represented attribute combinations, limiting diversity in minority samples.
approach: Proposes ProReGen using progressive residual generation inspired by Robinson's transformation to orthogonalize inputs, first learning majority samples then expanding with residual layers for minorities.
contribution: Demonstrates improved synthesis of minority attribute combinations across three benchmark datasets with controlled attribute correlation strengths.

problem: LLMs struggle with safety alignment, facing vulnerability to adversarial attacks and excessive overrefusal on benign sensitive queries, with current safeguards either rejecting outright or providing no guidance.
approach: Proposes WaltzRL, a multi-agent RL framework jointly training conversation and feedback agents as collaborative game where feedback agent provides safety suggestions that improve responses.
contribution: Significantly reduces unsafe responses (from 39.0% to 4.6% on WildJailbreak) and overrefusals (from 45.3% to 9.9% on OR-Bench) compared to various baselines.

problem: Vision-language models face computational overhead from extensive visual tokens, but existing pruning strategies either sacrifice feature diversity or increase hallucination without principled analysis.
approach: Conducts empirical analysis using effective rank for diversity measurement and attention entropy, revealing strengths of attention-based pruning on simple images and diversity methods on complex ones.
contribution: Proposes image-aware hybrid pruning achieving strong performance across benchmarks with reduced hallucination compared to diversity-only approaches.

problem: RL training dynamics in LLMs for reasoning remain unclear, with understanding limited to empirical observation of training trajectory.
approach: Develops theoretical framework via pattern-level and token-level analysis showing RL primarily optimizes sparse critical token subsets, reshaping reasoning pattern distributions under two reward types.
contribution: Explains RL training dynamics showing verifiable rewards enable convergence to optimal strategies when base reasoning is strong, while internal feedback initially improves then potentially degrades performance.

problem: Selective prediction for foundation models faces challenges across open-set taxonomy tasks with unbounded vocabularies: instability in visual-language embeddings and poor similarity calibration.
approach: Proposes memory-augmented PaPSP (MA-PaPSP) augmenting base method with retrieval dataset to reduce embedding variance via averaging nearest-neighbor pairs and using contrastive normalization.
contribution: Outperforms selective prediction baselines across selective captioning, image-text matching, and fine-grained classification tasks.

problem: Reasoning models exhibit overthinking with redundant steps, triggered by internal bias—an implicit preliminary guess about answers formed immediately upon encountering the problem.
approach: Identifies internal bias through empirical observation and counterfactual interventions showing removing input question reduces redundant reasoning and that excessive attention to input drives bias.
contribution: Demonstrates causal relationship between internal bias and overthinking across multiple reasoning models and tasks, though mitigation methods remain ineffective.

problem: Multi-task learning suffers from gradient conflicts causing unfair optimization and degraded performance when tasks have competing gradients.
approach: Proposes SVFair using Shapley value-based framework with geometric conflict metrics (VolDet and VolDetPro) to quantify task deviations and rebalance updates toward fairness.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse supervised and reinforcement learning benchmarks with controllable complexity.

problem: Understanding how neural networks efficiently learn high-dimensional features in the multi-index model setup remains theoretically open despite empirical success.
approach: Proves that two-layer network trained via layer-wise gradient descent agnostically learns target with o_d(1) test error using O-tilde(d) samples and O-tilde(d^2) time via power-iteration in first layer.
contribution: Demonstrates sample and time complexity align with information-theoretic limits up to leading order, proving optimality and that optimal results require first-layer training beyond O(1) steps.

problem: Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) fail on position-dependent dynamics and have spectral decay assumptions limiting practical applicability to many PDEs.
approach: Introduces KANO using dual-domain parameterization with spectral and spatial bases, including symbolic interpretability that overcomes FNO spectral bottleneck.
contribution: Robustly generalizes on position-dependent operators where FNO fails, reconstructs quantum Hamiltonians in closed-form symbolic representations with ~6e-6 state infidelity, vastly outperforming FNO.

problem: Vision-proprioception policies show inconsistent generalization: during motion-transition phases, the policy suppresses visual learning in favor of faster proprioceptive signals.
approach: Proposes GAP algorithm adaptively modulating proprioceptive gradient magnitude based on phase-guided transition probability estimation, enabling dynamic modality collaboration.
contribution: Demonstrates robust and generalizable vision-proprioception policies in both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation environments.

problem: Data-driven scientific models fail on out-of-distribution data but detecting failures in regression tasks lacks practical solutions, threatening deployment in critical fields.
approach: Proposes OOD detection via score-based diffusion models estimating joint likelihood of inputs and predictions, providing task-aware reliability scores.
contribution: Shows likelihood strongly correlates with prediction error across scientific datasets including PDEs and satellite imagery, providing step toward verifiable certificate of trust.

problem: Value-factorization methods for cooperative MARL lack robustness guarantees under environmental uncertainties from sim-to-real gap and model mismatch.
approach: Introduces DrIGM principle requiring robust greedy actions to align with robust team-optimal actions, deriving robust variants of value-factorization architectures (VDN/QMIX/QTRAN).
contribution: Consistently improves out-of-distribution performance on SustainGym and StarCraft with provable robustness guarantees while preserving scalability.

problem: Training graph neural networks for physical systems via gradient descent is slow, especially for large complex N-body systems, despite needing to respect symmetries.
approach: Replaces iterative gradient-descent optimization with random feature-based parameter construction for Hamiltonian Graph Networks, preserving physical invariances.
contribution: Trains 150-600x faster with comparable accuracy across diverse simulations including systems with up to 10,000 particles, with zero-shot generalization to 4096-node systems.

problem: Optimization on Riemannian manifolds lacks adaptive step-size methods with convergence guarantees without line search, limiting applications like Gaussian variational inference.
approach: Proposes RAdaGD, a family of adaptive gradient descent methods on general Riemannian manifolds achieving non-ergodic convergence guarantee O(1/k) under geodesic smoothness and convexity.
contribution: Provides first convergence guarantee for Gaussian Variational Inference without L-smoothness assumption and demonstrates competitiveness in numerical simulations.

problem: Existing safety benchmarks focus on low-knowledge misuse scenarios or simple classification, failing to assess model safety when handling scientifically sophisticated risks.
approach: Introduces SOSBench benchmark with 3,000 prompts derived from real-world regulations across six high-risk domains (chemistry, biology, medicine, pharmacology, physics, psychology), expanded via LLM-assisted evolution.
contribution: Evaluates frontier models revealing alarmingly high harmful response rates (84.9% for Deepseek-R1, 50.3% for GPT-4.1) demonstrating significant safety alignment deficiencies.

problem: 3D part segmentation only identifies visible surfaces, limiting utility for 3D content creation; extending to complete occluded parts while maintaining global consistency is challenging.
approach: Proposes HoloPart, a diffusion-based model with local attention for fine geometry and global shape context attention, completing incomplete part segments into full 3D parts.
contribution: Significantly outperforms shape completion methods on new ABO and PartObjaverse-Tiny benchmarks, enabling 3D part amodal segmentation for geometry editing and animation.

problem: Existing time series anomaly detection struggles with subtle anomalies like small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies using reconstruction or prediction methods.
approach: Proposes CS-LSTMs combining noise decomposition strategy with contextual dependencies and seasonal patterns, integrating time and frequency domain representations.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating effectiveness for robust time series anomaly detection.

problem: Most RL methods flatten return distributions to scalars, missing fine-grained structure of future returns and limiting applications in exploration and safe RL.
approach: Uses flow-based models to estimate full return distributions via flow-matching objective satisfying distributional Bellman equation, identifying high-uncertainty states via flow derivatives.
contribution: Achieves 1.3x improvement on average success rates across 37 state-based and 25 image-based benchmarks compared to prior distributional RL methods.

problem: Pedestrian trajectory modeling emphasizes social dynamics while neglecting environmental context, limiting realism in crowd simulation.
approach: Proposes EnvSocial-Diff, a diffusion-based model with structured environmental conditioning (obstacles, objects, lighting) and graph-based individual-group interaction module.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks, demonstrating importance of explicit environmental conditioning and multi-level social interaction.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models vary in local routing consistency—how well consecutive tokens activate similar experts—limiting understanding of which models suit expert offloading.
approach: Proposes two metrics: Segment Routing best Performance (SRP) and Segment Cache best Hit rate (SCH) to measure local routing consistency across 20 MoE LLMs.
contribution: Reveals trade-off between local routing consistency and local load balance, identifies domain-specialized experts contribute more than vocabulary-specialized ones.

problem: Current safety alignment methods rely on superficial refusal shortcuts or intensive supervision, failing to leverage LLMs' latent safety understanding developed during pretraining.
approach: Proposes AlphaAlign, a pure RL framework with dual-reward system: verifiable safety reward for justified refusals and normalized helpfulness reward, incentivizing proactive safety reasoning.
contribution: Enhances harmful content refusal while reducing overrefusal and maintaining task performance through explicit safety rationales, demonstrating simple pure-RL effectiveness.

problem: Solving infinite-horizon general-utility MDPs in single-trial regime—where performance evaluated on single trajectory—lacks practical solutions despite theoretical importance.
approach: Provides fundamental results on single-trial policy optimization including optimal policy class, casts as equivalent MDP, and leverages Monte-Carlo tree search for planning.
contribution: First approach solving GUMDPs in single-trial regime with superior performance to relevant baselines in experimental settings.
